All of the workshop's materials in one place. Each **module** pairs across four layers — a slide-deck **lecture**, a long-form **book chapter** (reading), a hands-on **tutorial**, and (for the analysis modules) the matching **Talapas HPC script**. Click straight through to any of them. Quick references live on the [Cheat Sheets](Cheat_Sheets.qmd) tab; supporting material — appendices, papers, datasets, communities — lives under [Additional Resources](Additional_Resources.qmd).

## During the workshop

::: callout-note
**How to read this table.**

- **P1–P2** — the optional **Tuesday (Day 0)** computational refresher: computer systems / HPC and R / the command line. Skip if you're comfortable with both.
- **00–08** — the laptop analysis modules, **Wednesday & Thursday**. Module 00 also gets you connected to Talapas through **VS Code + the Quarto extension** in interactive mode; SLURM batch is saved for Friday.
- **09–10** — the **Talapas HPC track**, **Friday morning**: the *same* `ifnb` analysis run as numbered R scripts submitted to the cluster as SLURM jobs.

Each row gives the **Lecture** (slides), **Reading** (chapter), **Tutorial** (view the HTML or download the `.qmd`), and — for the analysis modules — the matching **Talapas** script. P1/P2 and Module 00 have no Talapas script (—).
:::

## Bonus modules (11–17, self-paced)

Not part of the three-day in-person workshop — work through them on your own time.

::: callout-important
**Where each bonus module sits relative to the core pipeline.**

- **Run *before* the core (raw data → counts): Modules 11–12.** These take raw 10x **FASTQs** through Cell Ranger to the counts matrix (RNA) or peak matrix (scATAC) that the core Module 01 / Module 15 pick up. Most participants are *handed* a counts matrix by their sequencing core, so these are optional — but if you ever process your own raw reads, start here. The end-to-end version (raw reads → counts → full analysis) is the [Full Talapas run from raw FASTQs](Resources_Folder/Talapas_FullRun_FromFASTQs.html) roadmap.
- **Run *after* the core (downstream analyses): Modules 13–17.** WGCNA, trajectory & cell–cell communication, scATAC analysis, spatial transcriptomics, and FAIR data sharing build on a clustered/annotated object (or their own dataset). Modules 13 (WGCNA) and 15 (scATAC) use their **own datasets**; 14 and 17 run on the annotated `ifnb` object; 16 (Spatial) uses `stxBrain`.

The **Talapas** column links each module's script: the Cell Ranger `.sbatch` jobs (11–12) and the numbered analysis `.R` scripts (13–17), collected on the [Module 10 pipeline page](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_10_Talapas_Pipeline.html).
:::

After saving, **drop the trailing `.txt`** so the name ends in `.qmd`, then open it in RStudio (or in VS Code on Talapas). :::

## What's in each layer

- **Lecture** — the slide deck (reveal.js); the in-class summary of the topic.
- **Reading (chapter)** — the long-form prose "textbook" treatment, with worked examples and cross-references to the prerequisite [appendices](Resources_Folder/Reference_Material.html).
- **Tutorial** — a hands-on `.qmd`: **view** the rendered HTML to read along, or **download** the source to open in RStudio (or VS Code on Talapas) and run chunk by chunk (with *Think about it* prompts and collapsible answers). The laptop tutorials run on the laptop-friendly **`ifnb`** dataset.
- **Talapas script** — the *same* workflow as a streamlined script you submit to UO's **Talapas** HPC cluster as a SLURM job. The numbered analysis scripts and the `.sbatch` wrappers are collected on the [Module 10 pipeline page](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_10_Talapas_Pipeline.html).

::: callout-tip
**Recommended order.** Watch the lecture and read the chapter *before* working the matching tutorial: the lecture is the summary, the chapter is the detail, the tutorial is the runnable code, and the Talapas script scales it on the cluster.
:::

## Datasets

The laptop tutorials and the Talapas track both run on **`ifnb`**; Module 16 (Spatial) uses **`stxBrain`**, and the other downstream bonus modules (13 WGCNA, 15 scATAC) have their own datasets. Full download URLs, the expected directory layout, and a disk-space budget are on the **[Datasets](Datasets.qmd)** page. A quick data dictionary for the two main objects:

### `ifnb` — Kang *et al.* 2017 (Modules 01–08)

Human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), **\~14k cells**, 10x Chromium 3′ v1, loaded via `muscData::Kang18_8vs8()`. Eight lupus donors, each split into a control and an interferon-β–stimulated aliquot — so it has a **real condition** *and* **real biological replicates**, which is what makes integration, pseudobulk DE, and differential abundance meaningful.

| Variable (cell metadata) | What it is |
|---|---|
| `stim` | Condition — `CTRL` or `STIM` (interferon-β, 6 h). The two samples we integrate. |
| `ind` (→ `donor`) | Donor ID — one of **8** lupus patients; the biological replicate for DE / DA. |
| `seurat_annotations` | Author-curated cell type (CD14/CD16 Mono, CD4/CD8 T, B, NK, DC, pDC, Mk…). |
| `nCount_RNA` | Total UMIs (transcripts) detected in the cell. |
| `nFeature_RNA` | Number of genes detected in the cell. |
| `percent.mt` | Percent of reads from mitochondrial genes (added during QC; a stress/quality flag). |

### `stxBrain` — 10x Visium adult mouse brain (Module 16)

A **spatial** dataset: each observation is a **spot** (a ~55 µm patch of tissue containing several cells), not a single cell, and every spot keeps its **x/y position** on the slide. Two sagittal sections — **anterior** and **posterior** — installed via `SeuratData::InstallData("stxBrain")`.

| Variable / slot | What it is |
|---|---|
| `nCount_Spatial` | Total UMIs captured under the spot. |
| `nFeature_Spatial` | Number of genes detected under the spot. |
| `orig.ident` / section | Which tissue section the spot belongs to (anterior vs posterior). |
| `images` slot | The H&E image plus each spot's pixel/tissue coordinates, used for spatial plots. |
